blocks.raw:
<Tip>
Memory aid: **Test, Document, Approve, Correct**. Every material and system goes through this cycle: testing verifies specification compliance, documentation records results, the architect approves or rejects, and non-conforming work is corrected. If any step is skipped (e.g., no testing, poor documentation), disputes arise. The LEA tests your understanding of this systematic approach to quality control. Always ask: What testing is required? At what frequency? By whom? Documented how? Approved by whom?
</Tip>

blocks.raw: <WikiMistakeCard mistake="Accepting cylinder compression test results that marginally fail (e.g., 26 MPa when 28 MPa specified) without requiring either (1) retest of additional cylinders to establish trend, or (2) core boring to verify in-situ strength. The contractor pressures acceptance." correction="Establish acceptance criteria in Part 1: General before testing occurs. Typical: '28-day average must equal or exceed design strength; individual tests must not fall below 90 percent of design strength.' If marginal, require statistical analysis or in-situ testing (core boring per ASTM C42). Do not accept failures without documented justification." />

props.correction: Establish acceptance criteria in Part 1: General before testing occurs. Typical: '28-day average must equal or exceed design strength; individual tests must not fall below 90 percent of design strength.' If marginal, require statistical analysis or in-situ testing (core boring per ASTM C42). Do not accept failures without documented justification.
